title: I like, I don't like
summary: Say what you like and don't like with أُحِبُّ and لَا أُحِبُّ, and describe tastes: sweet, salty, spicy, bitter.
intro: أُحِبُّ means both 'I like' and 'I love'. Put لَا in front for 'I don't like': لَا أُحِبُّ. Things in general take الـ in Arabic, so 'I like coffee' is أُحِبُّ الْقَهْوَةَ, literally 'I like the coffee'. Another way to say it is يُعْجِبُنِي, 'it pleases me'; here the food is the subject, so the verb agrees with it.
objectives: Say what you like and don't like with أُحِبُّ and لَا أُحِبُّ
Ask a man and a woman what they like
Describe food as sweet, salty, spicy, bitter or delicious
Use يُعْجِبُنِي and تُعْجِبُنِي with masculine and feminine nouns

realLife.title: Koshari with Yusuf
realLife.story: Sami's friend Yusuf is visiting Cairo from Amman. Sami takes him and Daniel to the most famous كُشَرِي restaurant in town. Daniel loves spicy food and anything sweet; Yusuf doesn't like spicy food at all and prefers fruit.

mistakes.why: For things in general Arabic uses الـ: 'I like coffee' is 'I like the coffee'.

sentences.literal: not I like the food the spicy

mistakes.why: لَا ('not') goes directly before the verb.

sentences.literal: (question) you like the fruit, O Layla

sentences.en: I like koshari, and I like Umm Ali.
sentences.literal: pleases me the koshari, and pleases me Umm Ali
segs: I like it (lit. it pleases me; m)
and I like it (lit. she pleases me; f)
Ali (first name): Umm Ali is a bread pudding

mistakes.why: With this verb the food is the subject, and the verb agrees with it. Umm Ali is feminine, so it is tuʿjibunī.

sentences.en: Chocolate is sweet and coffee is bitter.
sentences.literal: the chocolate (is) sweet and the coffee (is) bitter

dialogue.title: Koshari for three
dialogue.culture: كُشَرِي (rice, pasta and lentils with tomato sauce and crispy fried onions) is Egypt's favourite street food: cheap, filling and vegetarian. For dessert many Egyptians love أُمّ عَلِي, a warm pudding of pastry, milk, nuts and raisins. When you admire something, say مَا شَاءَ اللّٰه.

lines.ar: يَا دَانْيَال، هٰذَا صَدِيقِي يُوسُف مِنْ عَمَّان. هُوَ فِي الْقَاهِرَة هٰذَا الْأُسْبُوع.
lines.en: Daniel, this is my friend Yusuf from Amman. He is in Cairo this week.

lines.ar: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا يَا يُوسُف! تَشَرَّفْنَا. هَلْ تُحِبُّ الْقَاهِرَة؟
lines.en: Welcome, Yusuf! Nice to meet you. Do you like Cairo?

lines.ar: نَعَم، أُحِبُّهَا كَثِيرًا! وَأُحِبُّ الطَّعَامَ الْمِصْرِيَّ أَيْضًا.
lines.en: Yes, I like it a lot! And I like Egyptian food too.
segs: I like it (f), I like her

lines.ar: إِذَنْ نَأْكُلُ الْكُشَرِي الْيَوْم! هٰذَا أَشْهَرُ مَطْعَم كُشَرِي فِي الْقَاهِرَة.
lines.en: Then today we eat koshari! This is the most famous koshari restaurant in Cairo.

lines.ar: مَا الْكُشَرِي يَا سَامِي؟ أَنَا لَا أَعْرِفُهُ.
lines.en: What is koshari, Sami? I don't know it.

lines.ar: هُوَ أَرُزّ وَمَكَرُونَة وَعَدَس، مَعَ صَلْصَة طَمَاطِم وَبَصَل مَقْلِيّ.
lines.en: It is rice, pasta and lentils, with tomato sauce and fried onions.

lines.ar: هَلْ هُوَ حَارّ؟ أَنَا أُحِبُّ الطَّعَامَ الْحَارَّ جِدًّا!
lines.en: Is it spicy? I really love spicy food!

lines.ar: أَمَّا أَنَا فَلَا أُحِبُّ الطَّعَامَ الْحَارَّ أَبَدًا.
lines.en: As for me, I don't like spicy food at all.

lines.ar: لَا مُشْكِلَة! الصَّلْصَة الْحَارَّة فِي زُجَاجَة صَغِيرَة عَلَى الطَّاوِلَة.
lines.en: No problem! The hot sauce is in a small bottle on the table.

lines.ar: مَا شَاءَ اللّٰه، الْكُشَرِي لَذِيذ جِدًّا! يُعْجِبُنِي كَثِيرًا.
lines.en: Wow, the koshari is really delicious! I like it a lot.
segs: I like it (lit. it pleases me)

lines.ar: وَأَنَا أَيْضًا، لٰكِنَّهُ مَالِح قَلِيلًا. أَيْنَ الْمَاء؟
lines.en: Me too, but it is a little salty. Where is the water?

lines.ar: يَا دَانْيَال، هَلْ تُحِبُّ الْحَلْوَى؟ أُمُّ عَلِي هُنَا مَشْهُورَة جِدًّا.
lines.en: Daniel, do you like desserts? The Umm Ali here is very famous.
segs: Ali (first name): Umm Ali is a bread pudding

lines.ar: طَبْعًا! أُحِبُّ كُلَّ شَيْء حُلْوْ، خُصُوصًا الشُّوكُولَاتَة.
lines.en: Of course! I love everything sweet, especially chocolate.

lines.ar: أَنَا لَا آكُلُ الْحَلْوَى كَثِيرًا، لٰكِنِّي أُحِبُّ الْفَاكِهَةَ.
lines.en: I don't eat sweet things much, but I love fruit.

lines.ar: إِذَنْ أُمُّ عَلِي لِدَانْيَال، وَسَلَطَةُ فَوَاكِه لِيُوسُف!
lines.en: Then it's Umm Ali for Daniel, and a fruit salad for Yusuf!
segs: Ali (first name): Umm Ali is a bread pudding

reading.title: Yusuf in Cairo
reading.ar: يُوسُف مِنْ عَمَّان، وَهُوَ يُحِبُّ الْقَاهِرَة. يُحِبُّ الْكُشَرِي، لٰكِنَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الطَّعَامَ الْحَارَّ. دَانْيَال يُحِبُّ الْحَلْوَى، خُصُوصًا أُمَّ عَلِي.
reading.en: Yusuf is from Amman, and he likes Cairo. He likes koshari, but he doesn't like spicy food. Daniel loves sweet things, especially Umm Ali.
segs: Ali (first name): Umm Ali is a bread pudding

quiz.prompt: How do you say 'I like tea'?
Complete: 'I like coffee' (lit. coffee pleases me).

completion: Wonderful! You can say what you like and don't like and describe how food tastes. Tomorrow: plurals of everyday things.
